why.C1: GRT-style recipe (random r, loss at sampled depth) is the one paper result that converges to a fixed point
why.C2: measured: R1..R8 equal, step angle 6.7 -> 0.1 deg
why.C4: u carries about one answer token
why.C6: not identity at init, carry grows +8.5 per pass

D1.title: S-FIX

why.C1: Loop-Think extrapolates with large Poisson R + zero-init, but on a parametric toy task; no grounded per-pass target
why.C2: pre-committed 4-5: placement unchanged, sampled-R loss can still be minimised by invariance on easy chunks
why.C3: 4 distinct d-256 layers cycled up to 8x
why.C5: single trajectory, decoder sees final plan
why.C6: identity at init, clamped carry, full BPTT through 32 layers

D1.vs_row0: Removes baseline defects 1 (not identity at init), 2 (train R max 4) and 4 (growing carry) and adds 4 distinct layers; keeps the loss placement, so it tests whether init + R alone caused R1..R8 = equal. Confirmed if E5 step angle stays > 1° past pass 4 and E4 agreement between passes 4 and 8 is < 1.

D2.title: LOOPFORMER-S

why.C1: LoopFormer 1B/25B: no stagnation (low cross-step CKA), elasticity; grounded via sg(u_L); not more-steps extrapolation
why.C2: main loss on R=L, shortcut distilled to the long endpoint: the exact asymmetry audit item 3 asks for
why.C5: decoder trained on long and (every 4th batch) short plans: usable at any R <= 6
why.C6: AdaLN warm-up risk at 25M (pre-committed penalty); two trajectories
why.C8: second trajectory + conditioning MLP; moderate trainer change

D2.vs_row0: Removes defect 3 exactly as LoopFormer does (main loss on the long route, short route distilled to it) plus defects 1, 2, 4; targets the measured stagnation directly ('concept drift'). Confirmed if E11 cross-pass CKA stays low and quality rises monotonically with R = 1..6 (E12).

D3.title: DEEP-SUP GROUPS

why.C1: strongest evidence: Diffusion-Timestep K<=160 -> 10,000; URM; TRM/GRAM 16 -> 256; grounded per-pass NCP target; puzzles not LM
why.C2: detached windows force each window to improve the previous state; equal per-pass loss is the evidenced pairing
why.C4: PQ unchanged; multimodal target may settle-then-wander
why.C5: heavier NCP weighting (mean over passes); X-bypass risk
why.C6: LN_h carry, per-window backward bounds memory
why.C8: per-pass logits + per-window backward: trainer change

D3.vs_row0: Replaces the loss that rewards R-invariance with detached windows that must improve the previous state, each pass supervised by the true next-chunk code (grounded). Confirmed if E11 per-window NCP improvement is ≤ 0 on average and hop/bind rise at R = 8–16 (E2).

D4.title: LOOPED-MoE + DELTA-RES

why.C1: Sparse-Layers (iso-FLOP LM): looped dense FFN is the bottleneck, MoE routing diverges across passes, 4x4 best; Delta-Res 220M-8B; no step extrapolation test
why.C2: as D1 (4) +1 for EBT's random per-pass step scale, the ingredient EBT found most important for gains that grow with steps
why.C3: state-conditioned per-pass experts + early-pass retrieval; CONDITIONAL: rises to 8 only if E11 shows routing divergence and E15 layer specialisation (shared pool untested — Sparse-Layers used per-layer pools)
why.C6: MoE at chunk rate: load balance noisy; shared pool untested

D4.vs_row0: Removes the 'same dense op every pass' invariance: state-conditioned experts make each pass compute differently, and a Delta Attention Residual lets pass r retrieve early passes instead of an overwritten S. Confirmed if E11 routing divergence across passes and E15 per-layer specialisation appear, with Delta-Res routing sharp (E14).

D5.title: K-PLAN

why.C1: D3's evidence for the schedule; Explorative Modeling says AR LMs are its hardest case (modest gains) — scored weakest per pre-commitment (K-plan novelty has the weakest evidence)
why.C4: K=4 candidate plans cover several valid continuations; leak <= 2 bits/chunk
why.C5: selector error = train/infer mismatch; multimodal middle unbounded until E13 measures it
why.C6: soft-min prevents seed starvation; more moving parts
why.C7: 24.2 % at R 4 (at the cap), training x1.49

D5.vs_row0: Adds what a single deterministic plan cannot hold: K = 4 candidate plans for a next chunk with several valid continuations, leak-bounded (≤ 2 bits/chunk), on D3's detached schedule. Confirmed if E13 NTP with the selected plan beats one-plan D3 and the selector's top-1 (E11) is well above chance.

D6.title: LOOPFORMER-MoE-DS

why.C1: inherits D3's evidence (Diffusion-Timestep 160 -> 10,000, URM, TRM/GRAM; grounded per-pass NCP) with the same puzzle-regime discount; Sparse-Layers (LM, iso-FLOP) for looped MoE
why.C2: D3's detached windows + LoopFormer consistency in the final window; the extra point over D3 rests on an ARGUMENT (state-routed experts give the carry a job X̃ cannot do), not evidence — capped at 9
why.C3: 4 distinct layers x 8-12 passes with state-conditioned experts; conditional +1 (to 8) only if E11/E15/E16 show routing divergence and layer specialisation
why.C5: heavier NCP weighting as D3; decoder sees only the final plan
why.C6: most moving parts of any design except D5: windows + MoE + per-window LB + consistency
why.C8: per-pass logits + per-window backward + MoE router/LB: largest trainer change after D5

D6.vs_row0: Attacks all three causes of today's 'passes don't matter': the loss (LoopFormer's distillation toward the endpoint in the final window), the optimisation signal (D3's detached windows, every pass graded on the true next-chunk code) and the computation (D4's experts routed on the state, so each pass computes differently). Confirmed if E16 shows window 2 routing differently from window 1, E17 shows drift in the final window, and hop/bind rise at R = 8–16.
D6.vs_D2_D3_D4: vs D3: experts routed on the state give the carry a job, so windows cannot just recompute from X̃ (D3's E13 risk). vs D4: D3's detached windows replace D4's sampled-R loss, which can be satisfied by invariance. vs D2: keeps LoopFormer's consistency where it is well-defined and gets per-pass variation from routing that exists at any R, so it is not limited to elasticity within the trained depth.

rules.C1: evidence without more-steps/OOD extrapolation caps at 5; +1 for a grounded intermediate target (per-pass NCP code or sg(final plan))
rules.status: C1/C2 are evidence-based projections, not results; the per-pass eval sheet (E1–E15) decides. D3's lead rests on puzzle/pixel-regime evidence (Diffusion-Timestep, URM, TRM/GRAM) — read 70.5 as a bet.
